paragraphs: My name is May, and I am eleven years old. It is Sunday afternoon, and my brother Pat is bored. He wants to play on the slide at the playground in the park. I have to study for my English test. So Grandma walks with Pat. Grandma does not know the new way to the park. I write the directions for her. The walk takes fifteen minutes. Pat has his red ball in his hand.

Go out of our gate, and turn left. Do not turn right. That is the wrong way, and it goes to the market. Walk along the street for five minutes. You will see a small hotel with a blue sign. There is nowhere to cross the street after the hotel. So please cross the street before the hotel, at the crossing. Hold Pat's hand when you cross.

Next, walk to the bridge over the small stream. Stop on the bridge and look at the water. The water is low and clean. Pat likes to see the fish. Then walk through the park gate. The playground is on the right, behind the big tree. It is safe, and many children play there. Pat will run to the slide. Grandma can sit on a bench under the tree. She can watch Pat from there. He is a small boy, but he is very brave.

Is the way easy for Grandma? I think so, because I draw a map too. It shows the gate, the hotel, the bridge, and the park. Grandma looks at it and smiles. "Thank you, May," she says. "Now I know the way." Pat is not bored now.
text.summary: Pat is bored at home on Sunday. May writes directions for Grandma to walk with Pat to the playground in the park, and she warns about the wrong way.
